youtube.baslik: Why shouldn't your hand cover your mouth in the Ling test? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: In the Ling test, the tester hides their mouth; if the child sees the lips, the result reflects speechreading, not hearing. But the hand should not be put right in front of the mouth, as it can distort sound; having the child look at a toy is better. Sounds are said at a normal conversational level, in random order each time, with silent trials in between, so the child cannot guess.
